title: Fuel Tank and Lines — 5.2L 32V Ti-VCT
introduction:
A fuel complaint needs more evidence than a gauge reading. I use the gauge as a stockroom report: knowing fuel is present does not prove the delivery system is getting it to the engine in the required condition and quantity. Vapor containment is another job again, so a fault there does not automatically identify a delivery failure.

Fuel tank and line diagnosis continues in the applicable Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis manual. That reference is not included here; this page provides no test setup, equipment specifications, measurements or result-dependent next steps. Its purpose is to point you to the correct diagnosis before testing or choosing a repair.

items.name: Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED) manual
items.detail: Access the diagnostic information applicable to the engine identified in this page’s title before selecting equipment or starting a fuel-system test.

edits.text: For fuel tank and line diagnosis, refer to the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED) manual and select the information applicable to this engine.
edits.why: The engine-matched reference is needed because pressure arrangements and test methods can differ. Fuel quantity alone cannot establish delivery performance or justify a component replacement.
